s1.syndrome_frame: Acute pelvic pain and urinary symptoms with a palpable mass
salient_findings: Multiloculated mass extending from the bladder dome to the posterior surface of the umbilicus
key_facts: 2-day history of burning on urination
Constant 5/10 suprapubic pain
Nocturia
Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, and changes in bowel movements
Last menstrual period was one week earlier
Physical examination revealed lower abdominal tenderness
Urinalysis with 10–25 WBCs per high-power field, moderate bacteria, and positive nitrites
Negative serum β-hCG, normal CBC and BMP
Cervical NAAT was negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis
Symptoms worsened despite antibiotic treatment
Chronic constipation with two hard, non-bloody stools per week
Contrast-enhanced CT scan showed a 4.0 × 3.3 × 6.8 cm multiloculated mass

differentials: Solitary fibrous tumor of the bladder
Clear cell adenocarcinoma of the bladder
Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder
per_call: Solitary fibrous tumor of the bladder
Clear cell adenocarcinoma of the bladder
Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder

shortlist.label: Urachal adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Multiloculated mass extending from the bladder dome, consistent with urachal remnant malignancy

shortlist.label: Urachal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Palpable mass and chronic symptoms, possible urachal remnant anomaly

shortlist.label: Bladder adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass invading the bladder dome, possible primary bladder malignancy

shortlist.label: Urachal diverticulum
shortlist.why_kept: Contrast-enhanced CT findings of a mass near the bladder, possible urachal diverticulum

shortlist.label: Adenocarcinoma of the urachus
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to urachal adenocarcinoma, possible diagnosis given the location and symptoms

raw.rationale: The presence of a large, multiloculated, enhancing mass extending from the dome of the bladder, as seen on the contrast-enhanced CT scan, along with the worsening of symptoms despite antibiotic treatment, suggests a malignant process. Urachal adenocarcinoma is a rare but plausible diagnosis given the location and characteristics of the mass, as well as the patient's chronic constipation and lack of response to treatment for a urinary tract infection.

rejected.label: Urachal cyst
rejected.why: A cyst would not typically cause worsening symptoms despite antibiotic treatment and might not show enhancement on CT scan.

rejected.label: Bladder adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the specific location and extension of the mass from the bladder dome towards the umbilicus is more suggestive of a urachal origin.

rejected.label: Urachal diverticulum
rejected.why: A diverticulum would be less likely to present as a large, multiloculated mass and might not cause the degree of symptoms described.

rejected.label: Adenocarcinoma of the urachus
rejected.why: This is essentially synonymous with urachal adenocarcinoma, making it redundant as a separate diagnosis in this context.
